scope: Actual isolated Git reproduction of raw-CRLF evidence normalization; not a listing captured from the failed hosted checkout. No application, workflow, classifier or clean-tree guard was changed.
head: 62a05adf12dfddb744a1e043c2bb4581c7b334e7
hosted_log_limitation: The classifier emitted a generic changed/untracked worktree error and did not list dirty paths. The earlier f066 run passed; this diagnostic does not establish why that run did not observe the problem.
result: Both core.autocrlf=false and true: five exact original JSONs dirty after raw checkout plus timestamp-only stat invalidation and --really-refresh; adding only the nested candidate produces refresh exit0 and an empty diff/status. All six original evidence files retain their exact bytes and Git blob IDs. Parent attributes and ignore committed blobs, and their initial checkout bytes, remain unchanged by the candidate.

reader_failures_retained.name: initial-reader-failure.json
reader_failures_retained.cause: Initial inline reader used strip() and removed the first porcelain leading space; the final assertion then failed.

reader_failures_retained.name: nested-parent-guard-execution.json
reader_failures_retained.cause: An overly strict reader guard expected canonical LF parent attribute bytes even under core.autocrlf=true. It was corrected to compare before/after checkout bytes plus unchanged committed blob identities.

initial_inline_reader_source: Captured verbatim from the recorded inline command; it was not originally executed as a file.
commands_scope: Linux Git 2.56.1 with two byte-preservation configurations; not a new Windows engine or native gameplay run.
reproduction_portability: The original reader and inventory retain exact execution paths. To reproduce elsewhere, bind the six inventory input paths to the referenced committed blobs and use a fresh diagnostic output directory.
